entries.description: Master clock output — stuck-low freezes all counters; stuck-high eliminates rising edges; both lose all sync (rolling/blank picture)
H_LO carry-out — fault prevents H_HI and V_LO from ever being enabled; kills all sync
H_HI carry-out — stuck-low/open prevents V_LO from incrementing (VSYNC never fires → vertical collapse); stuck-high speeds V_LO past normal rate (VSYNC fires too often → rolling picture)
H_HI bit 3 → HSYNC NAND input A — stuck-high widens HSYNC pulse (ghosting); stuck-low/open holds NAND input at 0 (HSYNC_n never fires → horizontal collapse)
H_HI bit 2 → HSYNC NAND input B — stuck-high widens HSYNC pulse (ghosting); stuck-low/open holds NAND input at 0 (HSYNC_n never fires → horizontal collapse)
H_HI bit 1 → HSYNC NAND input C — stuck-high widens HSYNC pulse (ghosting); stuck-low/open holds NAND input at 0 (HSYNC_n never fires → horizontal collapse)
V_LO bit 3 → VSYNC NAND input A — stuck-low/open eliminates VSYNC (vertical collapse); stuck-high forces VSYNC to fire at QC transition rate (rolling picture)
V_LO bit 2 → VSYNC NAND input B — stuck-low/open eliminates VSYNC (vertical collapse); stuck-high forces VSYNC to fire at QD transition rate (rolling picture)
Address bit A0 to decoder — stuck fault causes A0/A2 chip-selects to alias; ROM and POKEY respond at wrong addresses
Address bit A1 to decoder — stuck fault causes A1/A3 chip-selects to alias; RAM and EAROM respond at wrong addresses
